# Compute outer boundary of an N-ary tree

<!-- meta:begin -->
| Format | Difficulty | Asked at | Round | Topics | Last reported |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Algorithm | Medium | Uber | Phone screen | trees | Oct 2025 |
<!-- meta:end -->

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/compute-outer-boundary-of-an-n-ary-tree)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

A rooted ordered N-ary tree is provided via its root node. Every node stores an integer `val` and a list `children` of its child nodes, ordered from left to right; a node may have zero children.

Group nodes by depth, with the root at depth 0 and each child one level deeper than its parent. For a depth `d`, define `L_d` as the first node encountered at that depth when scanning the tree level by level from left to right, and `R_d` as the last node encountered at that depth.

The outer boundary path is the sequence obtained by walking from the deepest leftmost node upward to the root, then from the root downward to the deepest rightmost node. Let `D` be the maximum depth. First collect `L_D, L_{D-1}, ..., L_0`. Then collect `R_1, R_2, ..., R_D`, but omit `R_d` whenever `R_d` and `L_d` refer to the same node.

Return the values of these nodes in the order described.

For compactness, examples use nested lists: `[val, child1, child2, ...]`.

Example 1:

```text
Input: root = [80, [30, [10], [40]], [90], [60, [20]]]

Output: [10, 30, 80, 60, 20]
```

Explanation: At depth 2 the leftmost node is 10 and the rightmost is 20; at depth 1 they are 30 and 60; the root is 80. The path is 10, 30, 80, 60, 20.

Example 2:

```text
Input: root = [50, [70, [90, [10], [30]], [20]]]

Output: [10, 90, 70, 50, 20, 30]
```

Explanation: Depth 1 has only node 70, so it appears once; the right-side pass skips it.

Example 3:

```text
Input: root = [42]

Output: [42]
```

Constraints:

* `1 <= n <= 200000`, where `n` is the total number of nodes.
* The maximum depth `D` is at most `n - 1`.
* Your algorithm should run in `O(n)` time and use `O(n)` extra space.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

The outer boundary consists of the leftmost node at each depth, the rightmost node at each depth, and the leaves in left-to-right order, but avoid duplicates.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Perform a level-order traversal to collect the first and last node at each depth, and a separate traversal to collect all leaves.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Combine the left boundary (top-down excluding leaves), the leaves (left-to-right), and the right boundary (bottom-up excluding leaves and root) to form the final sequence.

</details>
